label: Text classification with leakage and drift checks
summary: A runnable reference for classifying text (tickets, documents, messages, reviews): TF-IDF with logistic regression evaluated optimistically and honestly, with duplicate threads, a post-hoc leak token and vocabulary drift built in.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 7 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints 6,000 documents with about 25% near-duplicates and a leak token in 18%. baseline.py reports macro-F1 0.91 on a random split with the leak token present, 0.44 on later months with the leak removed and whole threads held out, and a frozen model falling from 0.78 on the month after training to 0.44 in months 6-7 when new words appear. pytest reports 6 passed.

files.purpose: Synthetic documents with duplicate threads, a post-hoc leak token, confusable classes and vocabulary drift
TF-IDF with logistic regression, the leak filter, expected calibration error and the optimistic, honest and drift evaluations
Executable gates: determinism, leak removal, calibration arithmetic, thread-safe split and the leakage and drift checks

synthetic.description: 6,000 documents over 8 months and 8 classes: 25% are copies of earlier documents, 18% contain a token written only after the label exists, each class borrows 30% of its topic words from a neighbour, and from month 5 documents use mostly new vocabulary.
knobs: n_docs, n_classes, months: size of the corpus
seed: identical seed gives an identical corpus

pevi robuxo misape ledavi mibuka dazimi vixoda rokale fano x...
miro dakale buburo xoda letufa noda xogele samimi miromi buf...

slots.meaning: words and phrases most associated with each class
which conversation or document family a text belongs to
when the text was written, for time-based splits
probability that the top class is right

data.threshold: pytest -k 'deterministic or thread' passes; 15-35% near-duplicates; threads never straddle the split
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: A resolution token written after labelling is stripped from 100% of training texts

baseline.threshold: Recorded on later months with leaks removed and threads held out (the kit: 0.44 against 0.91 on the optimistic split)

challenger.metric: Gap to the optimistic number and drift
challenger.threshold: The optimistic split overstates macro-F1 by at least 0.25 and the frozen model loses at least 0.15 between the first and later test months (the kit: 0.47 and 0.34)

tests.pass: A resolution token written after labelling never reaches the model
A classifier that is always right at 90% confidence has calibration error 0.1
No thread appears in both training and test
Random-split macro-F1 is at least 0.25 above the honest figure
Macro-F1 drops by at least 0.15 between the month after training and months 6-7

lessons.trap: A random split with the leak token present
lessons.evidence: Macro-F1 looks like 0.91; on later months with leaks removed and threads held out it is 0.44.

lessons.trap: Copies of the same text on both sides of the split
lessons.evidence: About 25% of documents are copies; the kit keeps whole threads together.

lessons.trap: Using a field written after the label
lessons.evidence: A resolution token appears in 18% of documents only after the case is closed; it is stripped before training.

lessons.trap: Freezing a model and not watching vocabulary
lessons.evidence: A model trained on months 0-3 scores 0.78 on month 4 and 0.44 in months 6-7 when new words appear.

target: The label is the class of the document, assigned by the person who handled it; documents in the same thread share a label.

headline.baseline: macro-F1 0.44 on later months, leak removed and threads held out
headline.challenger: honest evaluation plus a drift alarm; the optimistic number was 0.91
